{"predictors": [
{"name": "R&D Expense Growth", "construction": "Calculate the 3-year growth rate of research and development expenses (Compustat item #46) and then rank stocks by this growth rate", "rationale": "Firms with rapidly growing R&D expenses are likely to be investing in innovative projects, which can lead to future growth and higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Employee Growth Momentum", "construction": "Calculate the difference between the 1-year growth rate of total employees (Compustat item #29) and the 3-year growth rate of total employees, then rank stocks by this difference", "rationale": "Firms with accelerating employee growth are likely to be experiencing increasing demand for their products or services, leading to higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Advertising Expense to Sales", "construction": "Calculate the ratio of advertising expenses (Compustat item #45) to sales (Compustat item #12) over the past year, then rank stocks by this ratio", "rationale": "Firms with high advertising expenses relative to sales are likely to be building brand awareness and customer loyalty, leading to higher future returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Property, Plant, and Equipment Obsolescence", "construction": "Calculate the ratio of accumulated depreciation (Compustat item #65) to gross property, plant, and equipment (Compustat item #7) and then rank stocks by this ratio", "rationale": "Firms with older, more obsolete property, plant, and equipment are likely to be at a competitive disadvantage, leading to lower future returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Pension Plan Funding Status", "construction": "Calculate the ratio of pension plan assets (Compustat item #74) to pension plan liabilities (Compustat item #75) and then rank stocks by this ratio", "rationale": "Firms with well-funded pension plans are likely to have lower future liabilities and higher returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Average Age of Directors", "construction": "Calculate the average age of the board of directors using data from proxy statements and then rank stocks by this average age", "rationale": "Firms with younger boards of directors are likely to be more open to new ideas and more willing to take risks, leading to higher future returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Institutional Ownership Concentration", "construction": "Calculate the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index of institutional ownership using data from 13F filings and then rank stocks by this index", "rationale": "Firms with more concentrated institutional ownership are likely to have more active and engaged shareholders, leading to higher future returns", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Customer Concentration", "construction": "Calculate the ratio of sales to the largest customer (using data from 10-K filings) to total sales and then rank stocks by this ratio", "rationale": "Firms with high customer concentration are likely to be at risk of losing a major customer, leading to lower future returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Supply Chain Efficiency", "construction": "Calculate the ratio of cost of goods sold (Compustat item #41) to sales (Compustat item #12) and then rank stocks by this ratio", "rationale": "Firms with low supply chain efficiency are likely to be at a competitive disadvantage, leading to lower future returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Geographic Segment Diversity", "construction": "Calculate the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index of geographic segment sales using data from 10-K filings and then rank stocks by this index", "rationale": "Firms with more diversified geographic segment sales are likely to be less exposed to regional economic downturns, leading to higher future returns", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}
]}
